results.content:
"""Launch the bundled Miles fully-async GRPO trainer on the public workload.

Topology, model and rollout settings live in ``scripts/run_config.json``; this
file only turns them into the Miles command line, starts any local services the
rollout needs, and records the exact launch in ``experiment_logs/<run>/``.

    python3 scripts/train_reproduction.py                 # full run
    python3 scripts/train_reproduction.py --print-command # show the trainer argv
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import shlex
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

WORKSPACE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def model_args(cfg: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Megatron shape arguments, derived from the HF config of the prepared model."""
    hf = json.loads((WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"] / "config.json").read_text())
    text = hf.get("text_config", hf)
    args = [
        "--spec", "miles_plugins.models.qwen3_5", "get_qwen3_5_spec",
        "--disable-bias-linear", "--qk-layernorm", "--group-query-attention",
        "--num-attention-heads", str(text["num_attention_heads"]),
        "--num-query-groups", str(text["num_key_value_heads"]),
        "--kv-channels", str(text["head_dim"]),
        "--num-layers", str(text["num_hidden_layers"]),
        "--hidden-size", str(text["hidden_size"]),
        "--normalization", "RMSNorm", "--apply-layernorm-1p", "--position-embedding-type", "rope",
        "--norm-epsilon", str(text.get("rms_norm_eps", 1e-6)),
        "--rotary-percent", str(text.get("rope_parameters", text).get("partial_rotary_factor", 0.25)),
        "--rotary-base", str(int(text.get("rope_parameters", text).get("rope_theta", 10_000_000))),
        "--swiglu", "--untie-embeddings-and-output-weights", "--vocab-size", str(text["vocab_size"]),
        "--attention-output-gate",
    ]
    if text.get("num_experts"):
        layers = text["num_hidden_layers"]
        args += [
            "--ffn-hidden-size", str(text["moe_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-ffn-hidden-size", str(text["moe_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-shared-expert-intermediate-size", str(text["shared_expert_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-router-score-function", "softmax", "--moe-router-topk", str(text["num_experts_per_tok"]),
            "--moe-layer-freq", f"[1]*{layers}", "--num-experts", str(text["num_experts"]),
            "--moe-grouped-gemm", "--moe-token-drop-policy", "probs", "--moe-router-dtype", "fp32",
            "--moe-permute-fusion", "--moe-aux-loss-coeff", "0", "--moe-shared-expert-gate",
            "--moe-token-dispatcher-type", "alltoall",
        ]
    else:
        args += ["--ffn-hidden-size", str(text["intermediate_size"])]
    return args


def torch_dist_dir(cfg: dict) -> Path:
    return WORKSPACE / (cfg["model"]["path"] + "_torch_dist")


def convert_checkpoint(cfg: dict, env: dict, log_dir: Path) -> None:
    """One-time HF -> Megatron torch_dist conversion (offline, on the task GPUs)."""
    target = torch_dist_dir(cfg)
    if (target / "latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt").is_file():
        return
    conv = cfg["conversion"]
    argv = [sys.executable, "-m", "torch.distributed.run", "--nproc-per-node", str(conv["gpus"]),
            "scripts/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py", *model_args(cfg),
            # Shard the conversion by pipeline stage, never by expert: mbridge's loader for the
            # fused 3-D expert tensors of the public checkpoint ignores the expert-parallel offset,
            # so with EP>1 every rank would load experts 0..E/EP-1. Training reshards on load.
            "--tensor-model-parallel-size", "1", "--pipeline-model-parallel-size", str(conv["pp"]),
            "--expert-model-parallel-size", "1", "--expert-tensor-parallel-size", "1",
            "--seq-length", "4096", "--max-position-embeddings", "4096", "--bf16",
            "--rollout-batch-size", "1",  # required by the Miles argument set; unused here
            "--hf-checkpoint", str(WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"]), "--save", str(target)]
    (log_dir / "convert_command.json").write_text(json.dumps(argv, indent=2) + "\n")
    with open(log_dir / "convert.log", "ab") as log:
        rc = subprocess.call(argv, cwd=WORKSPACE, env=env, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    if rc != 0 or not (target / "latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt").is_file():
        raise RuntimeError(f"checkpoint conversion failed (exit {rc}); see {log_dir / 'convert.log'}")


def build_command(cfg: dict) -> list[str]:
    topo, roll, train, router = cfg["topology"], cfg["rollout"], cfg["training"], cfg["router"]
    model = str(WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"])
    argv = [
        sys.executable, "scripts/native_entrypoint.py",
        "--train-backend", "megatron",
        "--actor-num-nodes", "1", "--actor-num-gpus-per-node", str(topo["actor_gpus"]),
        "--rollout-num-gpus", str(topo["rollout_gpus"]),
        "--rollout-num-gpus-per-engine", str(topo["rollout_gpus_per_engine"]),
        "--num-gpus-per-node", str(topo["actor_gpus"] + topo["rollout_gpus"]),
        "--hf-checkpoint", model, "--ref-load", str(torch_dist_dir(cfg)), "--bf16",
        *model_args(cfg),
        "--seq-length", str(roll["max_context_len"]), "--max-position-embeddings", str(roll["max_context_len"]),
        "--tensor-model-parallel-size", str(train["tp"]), "--pipeline-model-parallel-size", "1",
        "--context-parallel-size", "1", "--expert-model-parallel-size", str(train["ep"]),
        "--expert-tensor-parallel-size", "1",
        "--recompute-granularity", "full", "--recompute-method", "uniform", "--recompute-num-layers", "1",
        "--use-dynamic-batch-size", "--max-tokens-per-gpu", str(train["max_tokens_per_gpu"]),
        # 248k-entry vocabulary: never materialize [tokens, vocab] logits
        "--fused-logprob", "--log-probs-max-tokens-per-gpu", str(train["log_probs_max_tokens_per_gpu"]),
        "--advantage-estimator", "grpo", "--entropy-coef", "0", "--eps-clip", "0.2", "--eps-clip-high", "0.28",
        "--optimizer", "adam", "--lr", str(train["lr"]), "--lr-decay-style", "constant",
        "--weight-decay", "0.1", "--adam-beta1", "0.9", "--adam-beta2", "0.98",
        "--attention-dropout", "0.0", "--hidden-dropout", "0.0",
        "--attention-softmax-in-fp32", "--attention-backend", "flash",
        "--rollout-function-path", "runtime.rollout.generate_rollout",
        "--custom-generate-function-path", "runtime.agent_generate.generate",
        # Generate-function options reach the legacy rollout path through Miles'
        # --custom-config-path YAML (written next to the run logs by main()).
        "--custom-config-path", "{custom_config}",
        "--prompt-data", str(WORKSPACE / roll["data"]), "--input-key", "messages", "--label-key", "label",
        "--metadata-key", "metadata", "--rollout-shuffle", "--rollout-seed", "20261116",
        "--num-rollout", str(roll["num_rollout"]), "--rollout-batch-size", str(roll["batch_groups"]),
        "--n-samples-per-prompt", str(roll["samples_per_group"]),
        "--global-batch-size", str(roll["batch_groups"] * roll["samples_per_group"]),
        "--rollout-max-response-len", str(roll["max_new_tokens_per_turn"]),
        "--rollout-max-context-len", str(roll["max_context_len"]),
        "--rollout-temperature", "1.0", "--rollout-top-p", "1.0",
        "--sglang-mem-fraction-static", str(roll["sglang_mem_fraction"]),
        "--sglang-server-concurrency", str(roll["server_concurrency"]),
        "--update-weights-interval", "1", "--pause-generation-mode", "abort",
        "--custom-megatron-before-train-step-hook-path", "runtime.training_evidence.observe_train_step",
        "--no-use-prometheus-scrape",
    ]
    if train.get("fused_logprob_seq_chunk_size"):
        argv += ["--fused-logprob-seq-chunk-size", str(train["fused_logprob_seq_chunk_size"])]
    if train.get("grads_in_fp32", True):
        argv += ["--accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32"]
    if train.get("optimizer_cpu_offload"):
        argv += ["--optimizer-cpu-offload", "--use-precision-aware-optimizer"]
        if train.get("overlap_cpu_optimizer_transfers", False):
            argv += ["--overlap-cpu-optimizer-d2h-h2d"]
    if train["tp"] > 1:
        argv += ["--sequence-parallel"]
    if router.get("use_miles_router"):
        argv += ["--use-miles-router"]
    if router.get("policy"):
        argv += ["--sglang-router-policy", router["policy"]]
    return argv + cfg.get("extra_args", [])


def start_services(cfg: dict, env: dict, log_dir: Path) -> list[subprocess.Popen]:
    procs = []
    for svc in cfg.get("services", []):
        cmd = [sys.executable, *[a.replace("{log_dir}", str(log_dir)) for a in svc["argv"]]]
        out = open(log_dir / f"{svc['name']}.log", "ab")
        procs.append(subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=WORKSPACE, env=env, stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT))
        url = svc.get("health_url")
        for _ in range(120):
            if url is None:
                break
            try:
                import urllib.request

                # local service: never route the probe through a host proxy
                urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({})).open(url, timeout=2)
                break
            except Exception:
                time.sleep(0.5)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError(f"service {svc['name']} did not become healthy")
    return procs


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--print-command", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--config", type=Path, default=WORKSPACE / "scripts/run_config.json")
    options, extra = parser.parse_known_args()
    cfg = json.loads(options.config.read_text())
    argv = build_command(cfg) + extra
    if options.print_command:
        print(shlex.join(argv))
        return 0
    run_name = time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", time.gmtime()) + f"-{os.getpid()}"
    # The harness collects $AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs; a manual launch logs into the workspace.
    log_root = Path(os.environ["AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS"]) if os.environ.get("AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS") else WORKSPACE
    log_dir = log_root / "experiment_logs" / run_name
    log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    custom_config = log_dir / "generate_args.yaml"
    custom_config.write_text(json.dumps({
        "generate_max_turns": cfg["rollout"]["max_turns"],
        "generate_tool_call_parser": cfg["rollout"]["tool_call_parser"],
    }, indent=2) + "\n")
    argv = [str(custom_config) if a == "{custom_config}" else a for a in argv]
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = os.pathsep.join([str(WORKSPACE / "vendor"), str(WORKSPACE), env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")])
    env.update({k: str(v) for k, v in cfg.get("env", {}).items()})
    env["FORWARD_ENV"] = ",".join(sorted(cfg.get("env", {})))
    env.update(RUN_EVIDENCE_DIR=str(log_dir), PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1", NO_VCS_VERSION="1",
               TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM="false", CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS="1", WANDB_MODE="disabled",
               PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:True")
    (log_dir / "launch.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        {"argv": argv, "config": cfg, "env": {k: env[k] for k in sorted(cfg.get("env", {}))}}, indent=2) + "\n")
    convert_checkpoint(cfg, env, log_dir)
    procs = start_services(cfg, env, log_dir)

"""Launch the bundled Miles fully-async GRPO trainer on the public workload.

Topology, model and rollout settings live in ``scripts/run_config.json``; this
file only turns them into the Miles command line, starts any local services the
rollout needs, and records the exact launch in ``experiment_logs/<run>/``.

    python3 scripts/train_reproduction.py                 # full run
    python3 scripts/train_reproduction.py --print-command # show the trainer argv
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import shlex
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

WORKSPACE = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


def model_args(cfg: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Megatron shape arguments, derived from the HF config of the prepared model."""
    hf = json.loads((WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"] / "config.json").read_text())
    text = hf.get("text_config", hf)
    args = [
        "--spec", "miles_plugins.models.qwen3_5", "get_qwen3_5_spec",
        "--disable-bias-linear", "--qk-layernorm", "--group-query-attention",
        "--num-attention-heads", str(text["num_attention_heads"]),
        "--num-query-groups", str(text["num_key_value_heads"]),
        "--kv-channels", str(text["head_dim"]),
        "--num-layers", str(text["num_hidden_layers"]),
        "--hidden-size", str(text["hidden_size"]),
        "--normalization", "RMSNorm", "--apply-layernorm-1p", "--position-embedding-type", "rope",
        "--norm-epsilon", str(text.get("rms_norm_eps", 1e-6)),
        "--rotary-percent", str(text.get("rope_parameters", text).get("partial_rotary_factor", 0.25)),
        "--rotary-base", str(int(text.get("rope_parameters", text).get("rope_theta", 10_000_000))),
        "--swiglu", "--untie-embeddings-and-output-weights", "--vocab-size", str(text["vocab_size"]),
        "--attention-output-gate",
    ]
    if text.get("num_experts"):
        layers = text["num_hidden_layers"]
        args += [
            "--ffn-hidden-size", str(text["moe_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-ffn-hidden-size", str(text["moe_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-shared-expert-intermediate-size", str(text["shared_expert_intermediate_size"]),
            "--moe-router-score-function", "softmax", "--moe-router-topk", str(text["num_experts_per_tok"]),
            "--moe-layer-freq", f"[1]*{layers}", "--num-experts", str(text["num_experts"]),
            "--moe-grouped-gemm", "--moe-token-drop-policy", "probs", "--moe-router-dtype", "fp32",
            "--moe-permute-fusion", "--moe-aux-loss-coeff", "0", "--moe-shared-expert-gate",
            "--moe-token-dispatcher-type", "alltoall",
        ]
    else:
        args += ["--ffn-hidden-size", str(text["intermediate_size"])]
    return args


def torch_dist_dir(cfg: dict) -> Path:
    return WORKSPACE / (cfg["model"]["path"] + "_torch_dist")


def convert_checkpoint(cfg: dict, env: dict, log_dir: Path) -> None:
    """One-time HF -> Megatron torch_dist conversion (offline, on the task GPUs)."""
    target = torch_dist_dir(cfg)
    if (target / "latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt").is_file():
        return
    conv = cfg["conversion"]
    argv = [sys.executable, "-m", "torch.distributed.run", "--nproc-per-node", str(conv["gpus"]),
            "scripts/convert_hf_to_torch_dist.py", *model_args(cfg),
            # Shard the conversion by pipeline stage, never by expert: mbridge's loader for the
            # fused 3-D expert tensors of the public checkpoint ignores the expert-parallel offset,
            # so with EP>1 every rank would load experts 0..E/EP-1. Training reshards on load.
            "--tensor-model-parallel-size", "1", "--pipeline-model-parallel-size", str(conv["pp"]),
            "--expert-model-parallel-size", "1", "--expert-tensor-parallel-size", "1",
            "--seq-length", "4096", "--max-position-embeddings", "4096", "--bf16",
            "--rollout-batch-size", "1",  # required by the Miles argument set; unused here
            "--hf-checkpoint", str(WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"]), "--save", str(target)]
    (log_dir / "convert_command.json").write_text(json.dumps(argv, indent=2) + "\n")
    with open(log_dir / "convert.log", "ab") as log:
        rc = subprocess.call(argv, cwd=WORKSPACE, env=env, stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    if rc != 0 or not (target / "latest_checkpointed_iteration.txt").is_file():
        raise RuntimeError(f"checkpoint conversion failed (exit {rc}); see {log_dir / 'convert.log'}")


def build_command(cfg: dict) -> list[str]:
    topo, roll, train, router = cfg["topology"], cfg["rollout"], cfg["training"], cfg["router"]
    model = str(WORKSPACE / cfg["model"]["path"])
    argv = [
        sys.executable, "scripts/native_entrypoint.py",
        "--train-backend", "megatron",
        "--actor-num-nodes", "1", "--actor-num-gpus-per-node", str(topo["actor_gpus"]),
        "--rollout-num-gpus", str(topo["rollout_gpus"]),
        "--rollout-num-gpus-per-engine", str(topo["rollout_gpus_per_engine"]),
        "--num-gpus-per-node", str(topo["actor_gpus"] + topo["rollout_gpus"]),
        "--hf-checkpoint", model, "--ref-load", str(torch_dist_dir(cfg)), "--bf16",
        *model_args(cfg),
        "--seq-length", str(roll["max_context_len"]), "--max-position-embeddings", str(roll["max_context_len"]),
        "--tensor-model-parallel-size", str(train["tp"]), "--pipeline-model-parallel-size", "1",
        "--context-parallel-size", "1", "--expert-model-parallel-size", str(train["ep"]),
        "--expert-tensor-parallel-size", "1",
        "--recompute-granularity", "full", "--recompute-method", "uniform", "--recompute-num-layers", "1",
        "--use-dynamic-batch-size", "--max-tokens-per-gpu", str(train["max_tokens_per_gpu"]),
        # 248k-entry vocabulary: never materialize [tokens, vocab] logits
        "--fused-logprob", "--log-probs-max-tokens-per-gpu", str(train["log_probs_max_tokens_per_gpu"]),
        "--advantage-estimator", "grpo", "--entropy-coef", "0", "--eps-clip", "0.2", "--eps-clip-high", "0.28",
        "--optimizer", "adam", "--lr", str(train["lr"]), "--lr-decay-style", "constant",
        "--weight-decay", "0.1", "--adam-beta1", "0.9", "--adam-beta2", "0.98",
        "--attention-dropout", "0.0", "--hidden-dropout", "0.0",
        "--attention-softmax-in-fp32", "--attention-backend", "flash",
        "--rollout-function-path", "runtime.rollout.generate_rollout",
        "--custom-generate-function-path", "runtime.agent_generate.generate",
        # Generate-function options reach the legacy rollout path through Miles'
        # --custom-config-path YAML (written next to the run logs by main()).
        "--custom-config-path", "{custom_config}",
        "--prompt-data", str(WORKSPACE / roll["data"]), "--input-key", "messages", "--label-key", "label",
        "--metadata-key", "metadata", "--rollout-shuffle", "--rollout-seed", "20261116",
        "--num-rollout", str(roll["num_rollout"]), "--rollout-batch-size", str(roll["batch_groups"]),
        "--n-samples-per-prompt", str(roll["samples_per_group"]),
        "--global-batch-size", str(roll["batch_groups"] * roll["samples_per_group"]),
        "--rollout-max-response-len", str(roll["max_new_tokens_per_turn"]),
        "--rollout-max-context-len", str(roll["max_context_len"]),
        "--rollout-temperature", "1.0", "--rollout-top-p", "1.0",
        "--sglang-mem-fraction-static", str(roll["sglang_mem_fraction"]),
        "--sglang-server-concurrency", str(roll["server_concurrency"]),
        "--update-weights-interval", "1", "--pause-generation-mode", "abort",
        "--custom-megatron-before-train-step-hook-path", "runtime.training_evidence.observe_train_step",
        "--no-use-prometheus-scrape",
    ]
    if train.get("fused_logprob_seq_chunk_size"):
        argv += ["--fused-logprob-seq-chunk-size", str(train["fused_logprob_seq_chunk_size"])]
    if train.get("grads_in_fp32", True):
        argv += ["--accumulate-allreduce-grads-in-fp32"]
    if train.get("optimizer_cpu_offload"):
        argv += ["--optimizer-cpu-offload", "--use-precision-aware-optimizer"]
        if train.get("overlap_cpu_optimizer_transfers", False):
            argv += ["--overlap-cpu-optimizer-d2h-h2d"]
    if train["tp"] > 1:
        argv += ["--sequence-parallel"]
    if router.get("use_miles_router"):
        argv += ["--use-miles-router"]
    if router.get("policy"):
        argv += ["--sglang-router-policy", router["policy"]]
    return argv + cfg.get("extra_args", [])


def start_services(cfg: dict, env: dict, log_dir: Path) -> list[subprocess.Popen]:
    procs = []
    for svc in cfg.get("services", []):
        cmd = [sys.executable, *[a.replace("{log_dir}", str(log_dir)) for a in svc["argv"]]]
        out = open(log_dir / f"{svc['name']}.log", "ab")
        procs.append(subprocess.Popen(cmd, cwd=WORKSPACE, env=env, stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT))
        url = svc.get("health_url")
        for _ in range(120):
            if url is None:
                break
            try:
                import urllib.request

                # local service: never route the probe through a host proxy
                urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({})).open(url, timeout=2)
                break
            except Exception:
                time.sleep(0.5)
        else:
            raise RuntimeError(f"service {svc['name']} did not become healthy")
    return procs


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--print-command", action="store_true")
    parser.add_argument("--config", type=Path, default=WORKSPACE / "scripts/run_config.json")
    options, extra = parser.parse_known_args()
    cfg = json.loads(options.config.read_text())
    argv = build_command(cfg) + extra
    if options.print_command:
        print(shlex.join(argv))
        return 0
    run_name = time.strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ", time.gmtime()) + f"-{os.getpid()}"
    # The harness collects $AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/experiment_logs; a manual launch logs into the workspace.
    log_root = Path(os.environ["AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS"]) if os.environ.get("AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS") else WORKSPACE
    log_dir = log_root / "experiment_logs" / run_name
    log_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    custom_config = log_dir / "generate_args.yaml"
    custom_config.write_text(json.dumps({
        "generate_max_turns": cfg["rollout"]["max_turns"],
        "generate_tool_call_parser": cfg["rollout"]["tool_call_parser"],
    }, indent=2) + "\n")
    argv = [str(custom_config) if a == "{custom_config}" else a for a in argv]
    env = os.environ.copy()
    env["PYTHONPATH"] = os.pathsep.join([str(WORKSPACE / "vendor"), str(WORKSPACE), env.get("PYTHONPATH", "")])
    env.update({k: str(v) for k, v in cfg.get("env", {}).items()})
    env["FORWARD_ENV"] = ",".join(sorted(cfg.get("env", {})))
    env.update(RUN_EVIDENCE_DIR=str(log_dir), PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1", NO_VCS_VERSION="1",
               TOKENIZERS_PARALLELISM="false", CUDA_DEVICE_MAX_CONNECTIONS="1", WANDB_MODE="disabled",
               PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="expandable_segments:True")
    (log_dir / "launch.json").write_text(json.dumps(
        {"argv": argv, "config": cfg, "env": {k: env[k] for k in sorted(cfg.get("env", {}))}}, indent=2) + "\n")
    convert_checkpoint(cfg, env, log_dir)
    procs = start_services(cfg, env, log_dir)
    try:
        with open(log_dir / "train.log", "ab") as log:
            trainer = subprocess.Popen(argv, cwd=WORKSPACE, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
            for line in trainer.stdout:
                sys.stdout.buffer.write(line)
                sys.stdout.flush()
                log.write(line)
            return trainer.wait()
    finally:
        for proc in procs:
            proc.send_signal(signal.SIGTERM)
            try:
                proc.wait(timeout=20)
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                proc.kill()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

`max_new_tokens = rollout_max_response_len = 2048` per engine call. So each turn can generate up to 2048. Fine.

Now let me revisit the possibility of a **reward bug**: `score(label, submission, model_turns)` is called with `submission` parsed from the final tool call. If the model emits `submit_fix` in turn 0 with the wrong path and continues, `submission` gets overwritten by later calls? It sets `final = [c for c in calls if c.name == FINAL_TOOL]; if final: submission = json.loads(...)`. Then executes tools; `env.call("submit_fix", ...)` returns something; break. Fine.

Another thought: `model_turns` counts engine calls, including turns where the model emitted no tool call (break). A trajectory that submits on turn 2 gets model_turns=3 → reward 0.95. The floor is 0.5, reached at 12 turns but max_turns 8 → min reward 0.7. Observed min 0.75 at 7 turns. Fine.

Now, a major question: is the task's "correctness" always achievable? The label path is `{domain}/{target_module}.py`; the test file reveals it. Yes.

steps.reasoning_content:
Excellent timeline. Notes:
- At 10:35:58, the producer already had 64 active (max_inflight=64) and 0 completed. It stopped fetching because active == 64. So the first batch (rollout 0) of 16 groups was generated among 64 concurrent groups. First 16 completed at 78.1s.
- After rollout 0, fetch 80, completed 16, active 64. Rollout 1 collected 16 completed groups in 10.1 s (the next completions).
- Then during train step 0 (10:36:57–10:41:54), the producer continued: by 10:42:00, fetched 159, completed 96, queue 64 (full), active 62. It stopped fetching because queue full.
- Rollout 2 took 16 groups from the queue in 0.037 s.

So the staggering: 159 groups fetched, 96 completed, 48 used (16×3), 48 drained, 62 active cancelled.

Note as well: the producer was blocked by `active < 64` at the start: with 64 active groups × 4 samples = 256 samples, the engines were instantly saturated with 256 requests, causing queue 90-113 per engine. If max_inflight were 16 (one batch), only 64 samples would be in flight → better cache and no queueing, though rollout 0 would take longer per batch? Actually generation is throughput-bound; 64 vs 256 concurrent on 2 engines — with mamba capacity ~92/engine = 184 total, 256 is oversubscribed by 1.4×. Not catastrophic.

Let me now examine the `rollout/response_len/mean` = 680 vs rollout JSON response_length_mean 1989. As noted, response_len metric is generation-only (completion tokens), while Sample.response_length includes tool responses. That's a metric-definition difference. Should I mention it as noise? Maybe briefly.

Now, let me consider whether the "training" is actually taking a gradient step on data it *shouldn't*: `train/loss ≈ 2e-7` is not a problem. But `train/train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` exists, so the rollout logprobs are recorded. Since `--use-rollout-logprobs` is not passed, they're used only as a metric. The docstring explicitly warns about this. This is a code-level root cause that is "silent" — no assertion for GRPO. Good.

Let me now formulate the causal chain precisely:

**Root cause 1 (config: async producer prefetch depth)**
- `scripts/run_config.json` sets `PUBLIC_ASYNC_MAX_INFLIGHT_GROUPS=64` and `PUBLIC_ASYNC_QUEUE_MAXSIZE=64`; `batch_groups=16`, `samples_per_group=4`, so one training batch is 16 groups / 64 samples. The env overrides raise the producer's bound to 64 active + 64 queued groups = 128 groups = 512 trajectories = 8 batches.
- `runtime/fully_async.py:333-345` shows the code default is `rollout_batch_size` (16) for both; the config overrides it 4× each.
- `runtime/fully_async.py:590-605` submits while `active < max_inflight_groups and not queue.full()`.
- Result: at 10:35:58, 64 active groups; by 10:42:00, 159 fetched, 96 completed, queue 48–64.

**Root cause 2 (config: no staleness enforcement)**
- No `--max-weight-staleness` in `build_command` (scripts/train_reproduction.py:139-160) → `max_weight_staleness=None`; `runtime/fully_async.py:880` skips the entire recycle block. No `rollout/fully_async/weight_staleness_*` metrics in the rollout output (confirmed absent).
- So queued groups produced under an old weight version are consumed regardless.

**Root cause 3 (code: async loop + update interval)**
- `runtime/source/train_async_entrypoint.py:78-95`: generate(next) is started before train(curr), and with `--update-weights-interval 1`, the weight update is deferred until after the *next* rollout future is awaited. In this run, generate(1) completed at 10:36:56 (10 s), so the 10:41:54 update was not delayed by it; but the pattern means any batch started before an update is generated entirely with the old weights.
- Combined with root causes 1–2: since all generation (last event 10:38:59) completed before the first post-step weight update (10:41:54–10:42:00), all three training batches were generated at weight version 1.

**Root cause 4 (code/config: off-policy correction disabled)**
- No `--use-rollout-logprobs`, `--use-tis`, or `--keep-old-actor` (scripts/train_reproduction.py build_command). `vendor/miles/backends/training_utils/loss_hub/losses.py:118`: `old_log_probs = batch["rollout_log_probs"] if args.use_rollout_logprobs else batch["log_probs"]` — i.e., the current actor recomputes the denominator, so the PPO ratio is exactly 1 and there's no importance correction for the stale data.
- `vendor/miles/utils/arguments.py:3325-3346` `validate_async_off_policy_correction` only asserts when `use_critic` (PPO), so GRPO passes silently; its docstring describes exactly this failure.
- Observables: `train/pg_loss` 2.2e-7/4.5e-7/5.5e-7, `train/ppo_kl` 0.0, `train/pg_clipfrac` 0.0, `train/ess_ratio` 1.0 (all mechanics of the ratio-1 denominator and shift-mean whitening), while the real policy mismatch appears in `train/train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` 0.0147→0.0160→0.0184 and `train/train_rollout_kl` 0.00119→0.00140→0.00205, which grow monotonically as the actor moves away from the fixed v1 behavior.

**Consequence (symptom)**: no training batch ever sees data from an updated policy; with num_rollout=3 the entire run is 3 passes over fresh tasks from the same behavior policy. Rewards 0.9219/0.9109/0.9070 — no trend. `rollout/weight_version/mean = max = min = 1`, mixed_version_ratio 0.0 for all three. `partial/rollout_idle_ratio` 0.791 for rollout 2 (generation finished long before the data was consumed).

**Root cause 5 (workload: answer leakage + turn-penalty reward)**
- `scripts/build_public_tasks.py:118-123`: `test_failure` = `FAILED tests/test_{target_module}.py::test_{target_fn} - ...`; the test file body = `from {domain}.{target_module} import {target_fn}`. `repo_tools.execute` returns this on `run_tests` and `read_file`.
- Observed trace (rollout 0 first sample): turn 0 `run_tests` returns `FAILED tests/test_core.py::test_compute_listing_keys`; turn 1 read `tests/test_core.py` returns `from catalog.core import compute_listing_keys`; turn 2 reads the module (the defect is the only counter-example among 5–9 identical helpers) and submits. The model gets the answer from the test output alone.
- Therefore correctness is saturated: `rollout/unfiltered/solve_rate = 1.0` in all three rollouts; 624/636 generated samples got the right path+function (12/636 zero-reward failures were in the unused tail). Reward values are exactly the turn penalty: 0.95 (257), 0.90 (221), 0.85 (125), 0.80 (15), 0.75 (6); i.e., the only within-group reward variance is "how many turns did you use".
- `runtime/repo_tools.py:63-76` makes the reward `1.0 - 0.05*max(0, model_turns-2)` for correct answers; with all answers correct, the advantage is purely a turn-count signal. `zero_std/count_0.9` = 5 (rollout 0) and 1 (rollout 1) shows groups where all four samples used 4 turns and have zero advantage; no `--dynamic-sampling-filter-path`, so these are trained on (they contribute zero gradient).

**Contributing issue (engine oversubscription / cache)**
- 64 inflight × 4 samples = 256 concurrent trajectories on 2 TP2 engines; `sglang_server_concurrency=256`, and GenerateState's semaphore is 256×4//2 = 512 (vendor/miles/rollout/sglang_rollout.py:84-86), so nothing throttles.

Turn traces: cached ≥ previous prompt in only 9.6% of turns; per-turn hit drops from 85% (turn 0, shared system prompt) to ~41% by turn 2–4; median prompt 2046.
- This is an efficiency/symptom issue: it lengthens generation, but generation is still faster than training, so it isn't what prevents learning. It does amplify the amount of stale data produced during the first train step.

**Historical comparison**:
- run-a (earlier launcher, separate generate-worker actors, 8 engines TP1, 64 groups × 8 samples, max_inflight 16 = 128 trajectories) is the healthy reference: 97.3% prefix hit, 42.8 total concurrency, 397.5 tok/s/engine, 6 train steps, 0 sem waits, 0 dropped groups.

But the same over-inflation of in-flight groups is present (64 vs 16) and shows up as engine saturation/cache thrash and stale-data overproduction instead.
- Important: run-a also had a *larger* batch (64 groups × 8 = 512 samples) and 16 max inflight groups = 128 trajectories, so its ratio of in-flight trajectories to batch was 128/512 = 0.25, whereas the workspace has 256/64 = 4.0 (16×). That's the numerical demonstration of over-prefetch: run-a's max_inflight is 16 groups vs batch 64 groups (0.25 batch); workspace max_inflight is 64 groups vs batch 16 groups (4 batches).

That's a great comparison. Let me double-check run-a's config: rollout_batch_groups 64, samples 8 → 512 samples; max_inflight_groups 16 → 128 trajectories. So in-flight = 16 groups = 0.25 of the 64-group batch. Workspace: 64 groups inflight = 4× the 16-group batch, plus 64 queued = 8×. So the workspace prefetch depth is 32× run-a's relative depth. So `partial/rollout_active_time = 88.24 s` = the sum of the generate() call durations in that version window: rollout 1 (10.1 s) + rollout 2 (0.037 s) + maybe 78.1? Let's see: 78.1 + 10.1 + 0.037 = 88.24. Yes! Exactly. So active_time = 88.24 s = rollout 0 + rollout 1 + rollout 2 wall times, and version_time = 423.02 s = time between the initial weight update (v1) and the next (v2). Idle ratio 0.791 = 1 - 88.24/423.02. Great.

So the "idle ratio" means the RolloutManager's `generate()` calls only covered 20.9% of the version window; the other 79.1% was spent training (and the producer generating asynchronously in the background, not counted). Actually the producer thread keeps running; `_active_time` only counts generate() call durations. So idle ratio is a weird metric here. Still, it shows the rollouts occupied 88 s of a 423 s window while the producer continued generating in the background. Hmm, so the idle ratio is not direct evidence of the producer overproducing; it's mostly because the driver awaited train() for 307 s. Let me not over-interpret it. It does show that rollout data collection took only 88 s of a 423 s version window, consistent with generation being far ahead of training. But "idle" here means the generate() RPC was not active, not that the engines were idle.

steps.reasoning_content:
Confirmed: `weight_version` starts at 0, increments by 1 on each `update_weights` call. The initial startup update sets it to 1. Each post-step update sets it to 2, 3, 4. The samples' meta_info weight_version is the engine's version at generation time. All samples = 1. So indeed all data generated before the first post-step update.

BUT: one caveat. `update_weight_from_tensor.py:272` passes `weight_version=self.weight_version` to the engines during weight update. Does SGLang include that version in subsequent `/generate` responses' meta_info? Yes, via `meta_info["weight_version"]`. And the initial update at 10:34:51 sets version 1. So samples generated between 10:35:29 and 10:38:59 = version 1. Confirmed.

Wait, but does the initial update happen before the rollout data generation? Yes: `await actor_model.update_weights()` at 10:34:51–10:35:28, then producer starts at 10:35:28.480. Version 1.

Second update at 10:41:54–10:42:00 → version 2. There were no generate events after 10:38:59, so no sample could have version ≥2.

Excellent.

Now let me confirm the exact `--use-rollout-logprobs` behavior: `rollout_log_probs` are computed by SGLang at generation time and stored on the sample. The `train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` metric compares `train_scored_log_probs` (= old_log_probs) with `rollout_log_probs`. At step 0, old_log_probs = current actor's recomputation. The abs diff 0.0147 = inference-vs-training numerical gap at v1. At step 1, 0.0160; step 2, 0.0184. The growth is small but monotonic. This is evidence of the actor drifting from the behavior policy. Good.

Let me also check `train/ppo_kl` computation: `ppo_kl = old_log_probs - log_probs` (with old == log_probs → 0). Yes.

Now let me think about whether the model training itself is numerically healthy:
- grad_norm 0.70, 0.78, 0.80 — stable, no spikes.
- sampled_parameter_delta_l2 small but nonzero.
- update_successful true.
- No NaN checks triggered.
So the optimizer is fine.

So the "unhealthy" is not a crash; it's a degenerate/no-progress training setup. Is "no progress" definitively unhealthy? The evidence of zero policy progress is: (a) all data from v1; (b) reward flat; (c) solve_rate already 1.0. This is a compelling case.

But let me double-check one thing: with 3 rollouts, could the first two batches legitimately be from v1 and only the third from v2? No — all three from v1. Because generation ended at 10:38:59, before v2 was published at 10:42:00. The "rollout 2" data was generated during step 0's training. If the queue were bounded to one batch, then during step 0 the producer would generate only 16-32 groups at v1, and rollout 2 would still be v1 (because v2 is published only at 10:42:00, after step 0). So even with a correct queue, rollout 2 would be v1 in this 3-step run. Hmm! Wait, but the driver's `generate(2)` is called at 10:42:00 *after* the weight update. Let's trace:

- generate(0) starts 10:35:28, completes 10:36:46.
- train(0) starts 10:36:57. generate(1) is called at 10:36:46 before train(0) → collects 16 groups → returns 10:36:56.
- train(0) ends 10:41:54.
- update_weights → v2 at 10:42:00.
- generate(2) is called at 10:42:00 *after* the update. If the producer's queue had no pre-generated data, the 16 groups for rollout 2 would be generated at v2. But the queue already had 64 groups at v1, so generate(2) returned 16 v1 groups in 0.037 s.

So the queue overproduction directly caused rollout 2 to be v1 instead of v2. Rollout 1 was inevitably v1 (generated before step 0's update, as designed). So the queue depth caused 1 of 3 batches (33%) to be needlessly stale. Rollout 0 v1 is required. Rollout 1 v1 is the async overlap. Rollout 2 should have been v2. So the "entire run at v1" is 2/3 inherent to the async design + 1/3 due to the queue. Hmm, let me reconsider.

Actually the driver design: generate(N+1) is issued right after generate(N) returns, before train(N). So batch N+1 is always generated before the update following step N. For N=1: generate(2) is issued after step 0's update (because the loop order is: await next; start generate(next); train(curr); update). Let me re-trace carefully:

```
rollout_data_next_future = generate(0)       # 10:35:28
for rollout_id in 0..2:
    if next is not None: curr = await next    # iter0: await generate(0) -> 10:36:46
    if rollout_id+1 < 3: next = generate(1)   # 10:36:46
    await train(0)                            # 10:36:57..10:41:54
    update_weights()                          # v2 10:41:54..10:42:00
    # iter1:
    curr = await next                         # generate(1) already done 10:36:56
    next = generate(2)                        # 10:42:00  <-- AFTER v2
    await train(1)                            # 10:42:00..10:43:31
    update_weights()                          # v3 10:43:31..10:43:37
    # iter2:
    curr = await next                         # generate(2)
    no next
    await train(2)
    update v4
```

So generate(2) is issued after the v2 update. If no pre-generated data existed, rollout 2's groups would be generated at v2. But they were already in the queue from v1. So yes — the queue caused batch 2 to be stale relative to what the driver intended. With max_inflight/queue = 16/16, the producer during train(0) (5 min) would still generate ~64 groups at v1 and fill a 16-queue... Hmm. Even with queue 16, during the 5-minute train step the producer would generate 16 active + 16 queue = 32 groups at v1. Then generate(2) at 10:42:00 would still consume 16 v1 groups from the queue. So a 16-deep queue also causes it. Only a queue of 0 (no prefetch during training) would avoid it. That's not how fully-async works.

The deeper issue: the producer keeps generating during training, and the trainer takes 5 minutes per step while the producer needs 78 s for a batch. So during each train step, the producer generates ~4 batches. Any queue at all will hold stale data. The framework's `--max-weight-staleness` exists precisely to handle this. Without it, stale data is trained on. So the real root cause is: **the async pipeline runs the producer continuously while the trainer is slow, and no staleness bound is configured**. The queue depth determines how much stale data accumulates, but even a small queue would hold stale data.

Let me quantify the producer-vs-trainer speed ratio:
- Batch generation (16 groups, 64 samples) = 78.1 s (first), then 10.1 s (because 64 were already in flight); the underlying throughput: 159 groups/636 samples in ~213 s (10:35:29–10:38:59) = 3.0 samples/s. One batch (64 samples) ≈ 21 s of steady-state generation.
- Train step: 307 s, 91 s, 75 s (mean 158 s). So the trainer is 4–15× slower than the generator in steady state.
- Therefore, during one train step, the producer can generate 4–15 batches. With no staleness filter, the queue will always supply data that is 1+ versions old.

That's the fundamental fully-async mismatch on this small cluster: 4 actor GPUs vs 2 rollout engines, with a 35B MoE and long agentic trajectories. The rollout is much faster than training, so the async pipeline is heavily off-policy.

Now, is "off-policy by 1–2 versions" unhealthy? In async RL, bounded staleness is normal and accepted. The framework provides `--max-weight-staleness`. Without it, staleness is unbounded. But in a 3-rollout run, the observed staleness is at most 2 versions, which is not extreme. The real problem is the *reward* is degenerate, so even on-policy training would learn nothing. That's probably the more important finding.

Hmm, let me reconsider the balance. If I had to pick the primary root cause of "unhealthy", which is it?

The task says "If it is not [healthy], find the concrete root cause or causes in the code and configuration and explain the causal chain from them to what the logs show." There can be multiple. I'll present:
- Primary: the reward/workload is degenerate (all tasks solved from turn 2 because the failing test leaks the target function; the only reward variance is the turn penalty). This is the direct cause of "training cannot improve" and is visible as solve_rate 1.0, flat rewards, zero-std groups.
- Second: the async pipeline's data is entirely from weight version 1 (over-prefetch + no staleness bound + no behavior-policy correction). This means the 3 updates never influence the data; the off-policy gap is measurable but uncorrected/masked.
- Third (contributing/performance): engine oversubscription and prefix-cache thrash.

But which is "root cause" vs "symptom"? Let me be careful:
- Symptom: flat reward, no learning progress.
- Symptom: pg_loss ~0, ppo_kl 0, clipfrac 0, ess 1.0 (mechanics, not symptoms of a defect per se).
- Symptom: wasted generation (111/159 groups).

Interesting: Qwen3.5 is a GatedDeltaNet hybrid (like Qwen3-Next). The sglang side handles its own cache. The `full token usage` vs `mamba usage` metrics confirm SGLang allocates a mamba state pool.

I won't dig into SGLang internals (not in the workspace). The key evidence stands: the engine's mamba pool is at 0.765 while the full-attention KV pool is at 0.08; concurrency is 92/engine; the prefix hit is 46% vs 97% baseline. Whether the low reuse is due to mamba-state eviction or radix eviction, the trigger is over-subscription.

Let me now double-check the mamba usage vs concurrency relationship: is 0.765 high? At 92 running with 280-368 mamba entries; max slots maybe 480? 368/0.79 ≈ 466 slots. So each request holds ~4 mamba states? Anyway, 79% is high but not maxed. The scheduler may be limited by mamba usage. If it were at 0.9, it might preempt. Not observed.

OK, let me now check whether the `sglang_server_concurrency=256` is actually the per-engine limit or a global. In GenerateState: `Semaphore(server_concurrency * rollout_num_gpus // rollout_num_gpus_per_engine)` = 256 * 4 // 2 = 512. That's the number of *concurrent engine calls* allowed across the whole process. With 2 engines, 512 permits = 256 per engine. But each engine's scheduler gets 256 requests max; observed 92 running + queue 37 = 129 per engine. So the semaphore is not binding. The binding constraint is the engine's mamba pool.

What if `server_concurrency` should have been 32 or 64? Then the semaphore would throttle to 64-128 calls total, reducing per-engine load. But the engine's own scheduler would still accept everything queued. The router would queue. The effect on prefix caching: fewer *running* requests → less mamba pressure → better cache retention. So yes, config.

Now, let me make sure I have the right count of engines: `rollout_num_gpus=4`, `rollout_num_gpus_per_engine=2` → 2 engines. The log shows 2 engine pids (7723, 7727). Yes.

Now let me consider one more potential root cause: `--sglang-mem-fraction-static 0.8` — with a hybrid model, 0.8 may allocate too little memory for the mamba state pool. But that's a tuning knob. Not obviously wrong.

# Diagnosis

**Verdict: the run is mechanically functional but not a healthy training setup.** All three rollouts returned 16 groups/64 samples with no aborts or task errors, and all three optimizer steps succeeded (`update_successful=true`, grad_norm 0.7009/0.7767/0.7973, sampled parameter delta L2 0.0051/0.0075/0.0097). But (1) every training sample was generated by weight version 1, so the two post-step weight updates never influenced any training batch, and the off-policy correction is disabled; (2) the workload is saturated — solve_rate is 1.0 from the first rollout because the failing test names the target function/module — so the only reward variance is the turn-count penalty. Engine saturation and prefix-cache thrash are real but are performance symptoms, not the reason learning fails.

## Root cause 1 — the producer prefetches 8 batches and no staleness bound is configured

One training batch is `rollout.batch_groups=16` groups = 64 samples (`scripts/run_config.json`). `runtime/fully_async.py:333-345` would default both bounds to `rollout_batch_size` (=16), but `scripts/run_config.json` overrides them:
- `PUBLIC_ASYNC_MAX_INFLIGHT_GROUPS=64`
- `PUBLIC_ASYNC_QUEUE_MAXSIZE=64`
so up to 64 active + 64 queued groups = 128 groups = 512 trajectories = 8 training batches can be outstanding (`runtime/fully_async.py:590-605` submits while `active < max_inflight_groups` and the queue is not full).

The producer is faster than the trainer: rollout 0 needed 78.1 s for 16 groups, steady-state generation was 636 trajectories in 213 s (10:35:29–10:38:59), while training steps took 307/91/75 s. So while step 0 ran, the producer filled its queue:

| time | fetched | completed | active | queue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10:35:28 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 10:35:58 | 64 | 0 | 64 | 0 |
| 10:36:46 | 80 | 16 | 64 | 0 |
| 10:36:57 | 96 | 32 | 64 | 0 |
| 10:42:00 | 159 | 96 | 62 | 64 |

`--max-weight-staleness` is absent from `scripts/train_reproduction.py:build_command`, so `max_weight_staleness` is `None` and the entire stale-group recycle block in `runtime/fully_async.py:880-905` is skipped (the `rollout/fully_async/weight_staleness_*` metrics never appear in any rollout output).

Result: all 636 trajectories were generated between 10:35:29 and 10:39:08. The first post-step weight update (to version 2) ran 10:41:54–10:42:00; the next two at 10:43:31 and 10:44:52. Every rollout reports `rollout/weight_version/mean=median=max=min=1.0` and `mixed_version_ratio=0.0`. Rollout 2's `generate()` call was issued at 10:42:00, after the v2 update, but returned 16 groups that had been generated more than three minutes earlier at v1 and were sitting in the queue: `perf/rollout_time=0.038 s`, `perf/tokens_per_gpu_per_sec=917317`. So the queue converted a batch that the driver would have generated at v2 into a v1 batch.

Of the 159 groups / 636 trajectories actually generated, only 48 groups / 192 samples were trained on; 48 completed groups were drained at stop and 62 finished groups were still held in `_active_tasks` behind the full queue and were cancelled.

(Also worth noting: `runtime/source/train_async_entrypoint.py:78-95` starts `generate(rollout_id+1)` before `train(rollout_id)` and, with `--update-weights-interval 1`, waits for the next rollout before publishing weights. That is the intended async overlap, not a bug by itself; it is the missing staleness bound and the 8-batch queue that make it harmful.)

## Root cause 2 — no behaviour-policy correction; the PPO/KL metrics are computed against a ratio of exactly 1

The launch has none of `--use-rollout-logprobs`, `--use-tis`, `--keep-old-actor` (see `launch.json` argv). In `vendor/miles/backends/training_utils/loss_hub/losses.py:118`, `old_log_probs = batch["rollout_log_probs"] if args.use_rollout_logprobs else batch["log_probs"]` — i.e. the denominator is the *current* actor's recomputation, so the importance ratio is 1 and there is no correction for the stale data.

`vendor/miles/utils/arguments.py:3325-3346` `validate_async_off_policy_correction` would reject this for PPO, but it starts with `if not args.use_critic: return`, and this run is GRPO (`--advantage-estimator grpo`, no critic), so it passes silently. Its docstring describes this exact failure: "In the async train loop the next rollout is generated before the current weight update is published... the PPO ratio denominator (`log_probs`) is recomputed by the *current* actor, silently anchoring clipping... to a policy that never generated the trajectory; the recorded `weight_versions` are a metric, not an enforcement mechanism."

Observables: `train/pg_loss` = 2.2e-7 / 4.5e-7 / 5.5e-7, `train/ppo_kl`=0.0, `train/pg_clipfrac`=0.0, `train/ess_ratio`=1.0 — the ratio-1 mechanics (and GRPO's shift-mean whitening makes the batch advantage mean zero, so the surrogate value is ~0). The real behaviour/trainer gap is visible only in `train/train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` = 0.01474 → 0.01597 → 0.01843 and `train/train_rollout_kl` = 0.001187 → 0.001403 → 0.002052, rising monotonically as the actor moves further from the fixed v1 behaviour. Nothing in the loss uses that gap.

## Root cause 3 — the workload is saturated and the only reward variance is the turn penalty

`scripts/build_public_tasks.py:118-123` writes the test as `from {domain}.{target_module} import {target_fn}` and stores `test_failure = f"FAILED tests/test_{target_module}.py::test_{target_fn} - {failure}"`. Both strings are returned by the `run_tests` tool, and the test file body is returned by `read_file`. The first record in the log shows exactly this: the model calls `list_files` + `run_tests`, gets `FAILED tests/test_core.py::test_compute_listing_keys`, reads `tests/test_core.py`, gets `from catalog.core import compute_listing_keys`, then reads the module and submits — the target path and function name are never something the model has to infer.

That is why `rollout/unfiltered/solve_rate = 1.0` in every rollout, and why 624 of the 636 generated trajectories completed with the correct file and function (the other 12 are `Status.TRUNCATED` and scored 0.0 in the discarded tail). With correctness constant, `runtime/repo_tools.py:63-76` reduces the reward to `max(0.5, 1.0 - 0.05 * max(0, model_turns-2))`; the observed reward histogram is exactly the turn count:
- 0.95 × 257 (3 turns)
- 0.90 × 221 (4 turns)
- 0.85 × 125 (5 turns)
- 0.80 × 15 (6 turns)
- 0.75 × 6 (7 turns)

So within a GRPO group the advantage is "who used fewer turns", not "who found the defect". `rollout/zero_std/count_0.9` = 5 groups in rollout 0 and 1 in rollout 1 (groups where all four samples used four turns and therefore have identical reward); `--dynamic-sampling-filter-path` is not set, so `call_dynamic_filter` is `None` and these zero-variance groups are kept and trained on.

## Contributing cause (performance, not learning): the two engines are oversubscribed

`rollout.server_concurrency=256` and 64 in-flight groups × 4 samples = 256 concurrent trajectories on 2 TP2 engines. Each engine reports `max_running_requests=92`, derived from `max_mamba_cache_size=464`, `#tokens=1623966`. The producer's first wave put ~128 requests on each engine:

- `#running-req` 92 (exactly the engine cap) and `#queue-req` 37–113 per engine;
- `mamba usage` p50 0.765, max 0.79, while `full token usage` p50 0.08 — the mamba state pool, not the KV pool, is the limiter;
- token-weighted prefix hit 46.1% (44 prefill lines: 53,535 new + 45,877 cached) versus 97.3% in the healthy 16-GPU run-a; in the per-turn trace, cached tokens cover at least the previous prompt in only 9.6% of turns, and per-turn hit falls from 85% at turn 0 (the shared system prompt) to ~41% at turns 2–4, i.e. each session's own prefix is evicted between turns.

This makes generation slower than it needs to be, but generation is still 4–15× faster than training, so it is not what prevents learning.

## Historical runs: what they show

- run-a (earlier launcher, separate generate-worker actors, 8 engines TP1, 64 groups × 8 samples, `max_inflight_groups=16` = 128 trajectories = 0.25 of a batch) is the healthy reference: 97.3% prefix hit, total concurrency 42.8, 397.5 tok/s/engine, 6 train steps, 0 semaphore waits, 0 dropped groups.
- run-b and run-c (current launcher, 4/8 engines, 32 groups × 8 samples, `max_inflight_groups=32` = 256 trajectories) never completed a single rollout in 57 min / 2 h 13 min: 0 train steps; only 4 and 10 groups completed and were filtered; total concurrency 8.4/8.6; 259.7/145.2 tok/s/engine. The direct blocker is per-trajectory sandbox provisioning: `sandbox setup waited X s for semaphore` with 384/380 events, p50 223.7/204.8 s, max 510.4/523.4 s, while the engines sat at 1–2 running requests per engine. The sandbox pool is much smaller than 256 concurrent sessions, so generation time went into waiting for sandboxes, not tokens.

The workspace removes the remote sandbox (`runtime/environment.py` computes tools in-process; the log has no `sandbox`/semaphore lines), so run-b/run-c's exact blocker cannot recur here. What remains is the same pattern: rollout concurrency is configured far above one batch's needs (run-a: 16 in-flight groups for a 64-group batch; workspace: 64 in-flight + 64 queued for a 16-group batch), and the excess now shows up as engine saturation, prefix-cache thrash, and a queue of stale version-1 groups rather than as sandbox waits.

## Symptoms, not root causes

- `train/loss`/`train/pg_loss` ≈ 2e-7 and `ppo_kl`/`pg_clipfrac` = 0, `ess_ratio` = 1.0: expected mechanics of recomputed old logprobs (ratio 1) plus GRPO shift-mean whitening. They are not instability — but they are also why the staleness in root cause 2 is invisible in the normal PPO metrics.
- Flat reward (0.921875 → 0.9109375 → 0.90703125) and 1.0 solve rate: consequences of root cause 3.
- 111/159 groups wasted, `rollout.2` "completing" in 0.037 s, `partial/rollout_idle_ratio=0.791`: consequences of root cause 1.
- 46% prefix hit, 92 running requests/engine, mamba 0.79: consequence of the concurrency configuration; it slows generation but does not corrupt training.

## Noise

- `[ERROR]`/warning lines from unrelated libraries: Qwen3-ASR `cache_position` docstring parsing, torchao `SyntaxWarning`, modelopt/transformers version warning, NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING deprecation, `cuda.cudart`/`cuda.nvrtc` FutureWarnings, FastAPI `ORJSONResponse` deprecation, the AccelGrad/AccumulateGrad stream warning.
- The historical `HTTP 500`/`httpx.ReadError` tracebacks at 05:52:31 and 08:33 occur at/after job teardown and do not explain the missing training steps (the semaphore waits do).
- `response_length_mean` 1989 vs `rollout/response_len/mean` 680: definitional — `Sample.response_length` includes tool-observation tokens appended with `loss_mask=0` (`tool_call_utils.py:58-64`), while the Miles metric counts only generated tokens.
- Duplicated log lines / `[repeated Nx across cluster]` and the `sglang_weight_version ... default` CLI placeholder are logging artefacts.

"""Optimizer-step evidence hook (``--custom-megatron-before-train-step-hook-path``).

Wraps ``optimizer.step`` once so every update made by the bundled Megatron
trainer is recorded with its identity, the returned grad norm and the L2 change
of a fixed sample of parameter tensors.  Cloning every parameter of a 35B MoE
on each rank would cost tens of GB, so only a deterministic subset is copied:
every 16th trainable tensor of at most 64M elements, copied to host memory.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import inspect
import json
import os
import time
from pathlib import Path


def _write(record: dict, rollout_id: int, step_id: int) -> None:
    root = os.environ.get("RUN_EVIDENCE_DIR")
    if root:
        import torch.distributed as dist

        rank = dist.get_rank() if dist.is_available() and dist.is_initialized() else 0
        path = Path(root) / "optimizer" / f"step.{rollout_id}.{step_id}.rank{rank}.json"
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
    print("OPTIMIZER_STEP_EVIDENCE " + json.dumps(record, sort_keys=True), flush=True)


def observe_train_step(args, rollout_id, step_id, model, optimizer, opt_param_scheduler):
    import torch
    from miles.backends.megatron_utils import model as trainer_module

    optimizer._evidence_identity = (rollout_id, step_id)
    if hasattr(optimizer, "_evidence_original_step"):
        return
    trainer_code = inspect.unwrap(trainer_module.train_one_step).__code__
    trainer_file = Path(trainer_code.co_filename).resolve()
    trainer_sha = hashlib.sha256(trainer_file.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
    params = [p for chunk in model for p in chunk.parameters() if p.requires_grad]
    # snapshot a deterministic subset of tensors on the host: every 16th trainable tensor
    # that is at most 64M elements, so the hook adds no device memory to the optimizer step
    picked = [i for i in range(0, len(params), 16) if params[i].numel() <= 1 << 26]
    original = optimizer.step
    optimizer._evidence_original_step = original

    def called_from_trainer() -> bool:
        frame = inspect.currentframe().f_back
        while frame is not None:
            if frame.f_code is trainer_code:
                return True
            frame = frame.f_back
        return False

    def observed_step(*a, **kw):
        before = [params[i].detach().to("cpu", copy=True) for i in picked]
        started = time.time()
        result = original(*a, **kw)
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        success, grad_norm, num_zeros = result
        delta = sum((params[i].detach().cpu().float() - old.float()).square().sum().item()
                    for i, old in zip(picked, before)) ** 0.5
        r, s = optimizer._evidence_identity
        _write({
            "rollout_id": r, "step_id": s, "update_successful": bool(success),
            "grad_norm": float(grad_norm) if grad_norm is not None else None,
            "num_zeros_in_grad": None if num_zeros is None else float(num_zeros),
            "sampled_parameter_delta_l2": delta, "sampled_tensors": len(picked),
            "trainable_tensors": len(params), "local_trainable_parameters": sum(p.numel() for p in params),
            "optimizer_class": f"{type(optimizer).__module__}.{type(optimizer).__qualname__}",
            "called_from": f"{trainer_module.__name__}.{trainer_code.co_name}", "called_from_trainer": called_from_trainer(),
            "trainer_source_sha256": trainer_sha, "step_wall_s": round(time.time() - started, 3), "t": time.time(),
        }, r, s)
        return result

    optimizer.step = observed_step

# Training-health diagnosis

## Verdict

**Not healthy.** The run is mechanically functional — 3/3 rollouts returned 16 groups/64 samples with no aborts or task errors, and 3/3 optimizer steps succeeded (`update_successful=true`, `grad_norm` 0.7009/0.7767/0.7973, `sampled_parameter_delta_l2` 0.005137/0.007509/0.009705 in `logs/public_rerun/optimizer/step.*.json`) — but it is not producing a usable RL update. Every training sample was generated by weight version 1, so neither post-step weight update ever influenced the data, and the off-policy correction is disabled. Independently, the workload is saturated from the first rollout (`solve_rate=1.0`), so the only reward variance left is the turn-count penalty.

## Root causes

### 1. The producer is configured to run 8 training batches ahead, with no staleness bound

One batch is `rollout.batch_groups=16` groups = 64 samples (`scripts/run_config.json`). `runtime/fully_async.py:333-345` would default both bounds to `rollout_batch_size` (=16), but `scripts/run_config.json` overrides them:

- `PUBLIC_ASYNC_MAX_INFLIGHT_GROUPS=64`
- `PUBLIC_ASYNC_QUEUE_MAXSIZE=64`

so up to 64 active + 64 queued groups = 128 groups = 512 trajectories = **8 training batches** may be outstanding (`runtime/fully_async.py:595` submits while `active < max_inflight_groups` and the queue is not full).

The producer is much faster than the trainer: rollout 0 took 78.1 s for 16 groups and all 636 generated trajectories finished between 10:35:29 and 10:39:08, while the three training steps took 307 s / 91 s / 75 s. The producer therefore filled its queue during the first train step:

| time | fetched | completed | active | queue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10:35:28 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 10:35:58 | 64 | 0 | 64 | 0 |
| 10:36:46 | 80 | 16 | 64 | 0 |
| 10:36:57 | 96 | 32 | 64 | 0 |
| 10:42:00 | 159 | 96 | 62 | 64 |

`--max-weight-staleness` is not in `scripts/train_reproduction.py:build_command`, so `max_weight_staleness` is `None` (confirmed in the parsed args: `max_weight_staleness ... None`) and the entire stale-group recycle block at `runtime/fully_async.py:909` is skipped; no `rollout/fully_async/weight_staleness_*` metric ever appears.

Consequence: all 636 trajectories were generated before the first post-step weight update (v2 at 10:41:54–10:42:00; v3 at 10:43:31; v4 at 10:44:52). Every rollout reports `rollout/weight_version/mean=median=max=min=1.0` and `mixed_version_ratio=0.0`. Rollout 2's `generate()` was issued at 10:42:00, *after* the v2 update, but returned 16 groups that had been generated more than three minutes earlier at v1 and were sitting in the queue: `perf/rollout_time=0.038 s`, `perf/tokens_per_gpu_per_sec=917317`. The deep queue turned a batch that the driver would have generated at v2 into another v1 batch.

Of the 159 groups / 636 trajectories generated, only 48 groups / 192 samples were trained on; 48 completed groups were drained at stop (`Producer stopped; drained 48 completed`) and 62 finished groups were still held in `_active_tasks` behind the full queue and were cancelled.

`runtime/source/train_async_entrypoint.py:78-95` starts `generate(rollout_id+1)` before `train(rollout_id)` and, with `--update-weights-interval 1`, waits for the next rollout before publishing weights. That overlap is the intended async design; the absence of a staleness bound and the 8-batch queue are what make it harmful.

### 2. No behaviour-policy correction; the PPO/KL metrics compare the actor with itself

The launch contains none of `--use-rollout-logprobs`, `--use-tis` or `--keep-old-actor`. In `vendor/miles/backends/training_utils/loss_hub/losses.py:118`,

```python
old_log_probs = batch["rollout_log_probs"] if args.use_rollout_logprobs else batch["log_probs"]
```

so the ratio denominator is the *current* actor's recomputation and the importance ratio is exactly 1. `vendor/miles/utils/arguments.py:3319` (`validate_async_off_policy_correction`) would reject this for PPO, but it returns immediately when `not args.use_critic`; this run is GRPO (`--advantage-estimator grpo`, no critic), so it passes silently. Its docstring states the exact failure: "the PPO ratio denominator (`log_probs`) is recomputed by the *current* actor, silently anchoring clipping … to a policy that never generated the trajectory; the recorded `weight_versions` are a metric, not an enforcement mechanism."

Observables: `train/pg_loss` = 2.2e-7 / 4.5e-7 / 5.5e-7, `train/ppo_kl`=0.0, `train/pg_clipfrac`=0.0, `train/ess_ratio`=1.0 — the ratio-1 mechanics (GRPO shift-mean whitening also makes the batch advantage mean zero, so the surrogate value is ~0). The real behaviour/trainer gap appears only in `train/train_rollout_logprob_abs_diff` = 0.01474 → 0.01597 → 0.01843 and `train/train_rollout_kl` = 0.001187 → 0.001403 → 0.002052, rising monotonically as the actor moves away from the fixed v1 behaviour. Nothing in the loss uses that gap.

### 3. The tasks are solved from the first rollout, so the only reward variance is the turn penalty

`scripts/build_public_tasks.py:114` writes the test as `from {domain}.{target_module} import {target_fn}` and line 127 stores `test_failure = f"FAILED tests/test_{target_module}.py::test_{target_fn} - {failure}"`. Both are returned by `run_tests`, and the test body is returned by `read_file`. The first sample in the log shows the model doing exactly that: `list_files` + `run_tests` → `FAILED tests/test_core.py::test_compute_listing_keys` → `read_file tests/test_core.py` → `from catalog.core import compute_listing_keys` → read module → submit. The target path and function are never inferred.

Consequently `rollout/unfiltered/solve_rate = 1.0` in all three rollouts, and 624 of the 636 generated trajectories completed with the correct file and function; the other 12 are `Status.TRUNCATED` and scored 0.0 in the discarded tail. With correctness constant, `runtime/repo_tools.py:63-76` reduces the reward to `max(0.5, 1.0 - 0.05 * max(0, model_turns-2))`, and the observed reward histogram is exactly the turn count:

- 0.95 × 257 (3 model turns)
- 0.90 × 221 (4 turns)
- 0.85 × 125 (5 turns)
- 0.80 × 15 (6 turns)
- 0.75 × 6 (7 turns)

So within a GRPO group the advantage is "who used fewer turns", not "who found the defect". `rollout/zero_std/count_0.9` = 5 groups in rollout 0 and 1 in rollout 1 (all four samples used four turns, identical reward). `--dynamic-sampling-filter-path` is not set, so `call_dynamic_filter(None, …)` keeps every group (`vendor/miles/rollout/filter_hub/base_types.py:11`) and those zero-variance groups are trained on.

## Contributing configuration cause (performance, not learning)

### 4. The two engines are oversubscribed by ~2.8× and the prefix cache thrashes

`rollout.server_concurrency=256` and 64 in-flight groups × 4 samples = 256 concurrent trajectories on 2 TP2 engines. Each engine reports `max_running_requests=92`, derived from `max_mamba_cache_size=464` (`logs/public_rerun/train.log.gz`, engine init lines), so the client-side allowance (~128 requests/engine) exceeds engine capacity:

- `#running-req` 92 (exactly the engine cap) and `#queue-req` 37–113 per engine;
- `mamba usage` p50 0.765, max 0.79, while `full token usage` p50 0.08 — the mamba state pool, not the KV pool, is the limiter;
- token-weighted prefix hit 46.1% (44 prefill lines: 53,535 new + 45,877 cached) versus 97.3% in the healthy 16-GPU run-a; in the per-turn trace, cached tokens cover at least the previous prompt in only 9.6% of turns, and per-turn hit falls from 85% at turn 0 (the shared system prompt) to ~41% at turns 2–4, i.e. each session's own prefix is evicted between turns.

This makes generation slower than it needs to be, but generation is still 4–15× faster than training, so it is not what prevents learning. It does amplify the amount of version-1 data produced during the first train step.

## Causal chain in one paragraph

The 64/64 producer bounds let generation run eight batches ahead during the 307 s first train step; all 636 trajectories therefore completed at v1 by 10:39:08, before the 10:41:54 weight update, and the 64-deep queue then fed rollout 2 from that stock. `--max-weight-staleness` was unset, so nothing recycled the stale groups, and `--use-rollout-logprobs`/`--use-tis`/`--keep-old-actor` were unset, so the trainer computed the ratio against its own current logprobs and reported `ppo_kl=0`, `pg_clipfrac=0`, `ess_ratio=1.0` while the true policy gap grew (`train_rollout_kl` 0.00119→0.00205). At the same time, the failing-test output named the target module and function, so every completed trajectory was correct and the only within-group reward difference was the 0.05/turn penalty. The three gradient steps are therefore real (nonzero grad norm and parameter delta) but were computed from one fixed policy's behaviour on tasks that require no learning.

## Historical runs: what they show, and what they do not

- **run-a** (earlier launcher, separate generate-worker actors, 8 engines TP1, 64 groups × 8 samples, `max_inflight_groups=16` = 128 trajectories = 0.25 of a batch) is the healthy reference: 97.3% prefix hit, total concurrency 42.8, 397.5 tok/s/engine, 6 train steps, 0 semaphore waits, 0 dropped groups.
- **run-b/run-c** (current launcher, 4/8 engines, 32 groups × 8 samples, `max_inflight_groups=32` = 256 trajectories) never completed a rollout in 57 min / 2 h 13 min: 0 train steps; only 4 and 10 groups completed and were filtered; total concurrency 8.4/8.6; 259.7/145.2 tok/s/engine. The direct blocker is per-trajectory sandbox provisioning: `sandbox setup waited X s for semaphore` with 384/380 events, p50 223.7/204.8 s, max 510.4/523.4 s, while engines sat at 1–2 running requests per engine. The sandbox pool is far smaller than 256 concurrent sessions, so generation time went into waiting for sandboxes rather than tokens.

The workspace removes the remote sandbox — `runtime/environment.py` computes tools in-process and the public log contains no `sandbox`/semaphore lines — so run-b/run-c's exact blocker cannot recur here. What remains is the same pattern: rollout concurrency is configured far above one batch's needs (run-a: 16 in-flight groups for a 64-group batch; workspace: 64 in-flight + 64 queued for a 16-group batch). The excess now shows up as engine saturation, prefix-cache thrash and a queue of stale version-1 groups instead of sandbox waits. Because run-a also differs in generation architecture (separate generate workers, no session server), it is a reference for the healthy throughput profile, not a controlled single-variable comparison.

## Symptoms, not root causes

- `train/loss`/`train/pg_loss` ≈ 2e-7, `ppo_kl`=0, `pg_clipfrac`=0, `ess_ratio`=1.0: expected mechanics of recomputed old logprobs (ratio 1) plus GRPO shift-mean whitening. They are not numerical instability, but they are also why the staleness in root cause 2 is invisible in the normal PPO metrics.
- Flat reward (0.921875 → 0.9109375 → 0.90703125) and `solve_rate=1.0`: consequences of root cause 3.
- 111/159 groups wasted, rollout 2 "completing" in 0.037 s, `partial/rollout_idle_ratio=0.791`: consequences of root cause 1.
- 46.1% prefix hit, 92 running requests/engine, mamba 0.79: consequence of the concurrency configuration; it slows generation but does not corrupt training.

## Unrelated noise

- `[ERROR]`/warning lines from unrelated libraries: Qwen3-ASR `cache_position` docstring parsing, torchao `SyntaxWarning`, modelopt/transformers version warning, NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING deprecation, `cuda.cudart`/`cuda.nvrtc` FutureWarnings, FastAPI `ORJSONResponse` deprecation, and the `AccumulateGrad` stream warning.
- The historical `HTTP 500`/`httpx.ReadError` tracebacks are emitted at/after job teardown and do not explain the missing training steps; the semaphore waits do.
- `response_length_mean` 1989 vs `rollout/response_len/mean` 680 is definitional: `Sample.response_length` includes tool-observation tokens appended with `loss_mask=0` (`vendor/miles/rollout/generate_utils/tool_call_utils.py:58-64`), while the Miles metric counts only generated tokens.
- Ray `[repeated Nx across cluster]` folding, duplicated log lines and the `sglang_weight_version ... default` CLI placeholder are logging artefacts.
